correctness.rationale: Classify all maximal abelian subgroups as A=<x> and n order-four B_i=<x^iy> meeting at the center Z=<x^n>. Their left coset cover has two A-coset apices and n² small cosets; every nonempty intersection of principal downsets has its terminal intersection coset fixed by stabilizer, so the equivariant nerve lemma applies. The nerve is a union of row and column simplices, and the explicit second-largest-barycentric-coordinate contraction fixes shared vertices, yielding a G-equivariant K_{2,n²}. Orient U/V-to-e edges: cycles are exactly sum-zero integer e-coefficients with sign reversal when G swaps U,V. Stabilizers fix n² small cosets on Z, none on A\Z, and n off A; traces follow, and edge-pair orbits collapse the quotient graph to a tree. Independent group-law/coset/stabilizer enumeration for n=2,3,4,5 reproduced these cardinalities and character cases; proof, not finite extrapolation, handles n>=2.
residual_risks: The contraction and nerve-equivariance are for left regular translation, not all automorphisms or Borel quotients.
